82: def loop_area(B, M):
83:     """Area do laco de histerese fechado, via integral de linha
84:     (formula do shoelace aplicada a curva fechada no plano B-M).
85:     Equivalente a integral de M dB ao longo do ciclo completo."""
86:     B = np.asarray(B)
87:     M = np.asarray(M)
88:     # garante que o ciclo esta fechado (ultimo ponto ~ primeiro ponto);
89:     # se nao estiver exatamente fechado (ruido numerico no ultimo passo),
90:     # fecha explicitamente para a integral de linha nao vazar area espuria.
91:     if not np.isclose(B[0], B[-1], atol=1e-9) or not np.isclose(M[0], M[-1], atol=1e-6):
92:         B = np.append(B, B[0])
93:         M = np.append(M, M[0])
94:     # area de poligono fechado no plano (B, M):
95:     area = 0.5 * np.abs(np.sum(B[:-1] * M[1:] - B[1:] * M[:-1]))
96:     return area
97:

99: def find_zero_crossings(x, y):
100:     """Retorna os valores de x onde y cruza zero, via interpolacao linear
101:     entre pontos consecutivos de sinais opostos."""
102:     sign = np.sign(y)
103:     sign[sign == 0] = 1  # evita falsos cruzamentos em y exatamente 0
104:     idx = np.where(np.diff(sign) != 0)[0]
105:     crossings = []
106:     for i in idx:
107:         x0, x1 = x[i], x[i + 1]
108:         y0, y1 = y[i], y[i + 1]
109:         if y1 == y0:
110:             continue
111:         xc = x0 + (0.0 - y0) * (x1 - x0) / (y1 - y0)
112:         crossings.append(xc)
113:     return np.array(crossings)
114: 
115: 
116: def coercivity_and_remanence(B, M):
117:     """
118:     Bc (campo coercivo)  : valor de |B| onde M cruza zero (media dos
119:                             cruzamentos encontrados, ja que o laco tem
120:                             mais de um cruzamento ao longo do ciclo).
121:     Mr (remanencia)       : valor de |M| onde B cruza zero.
122:     """
123:     B = np.asarray(B)
124:     M = np.asarray(M)
125: 
126:     # Bc: onde M(t) cruza zero -> le o B correspondente
127:     M_crossings_idx_B = find_zero_crossings(B, M)  # x=B, y=M -> retorna B onde M=0... espera, precisamos inverter
128:     # find_zero_crossings(x,y) acha x onde y=0. Para Bc queremos o valor de
129:     # B onde M=0 -> x deve ser B, y deve ser M. Jah esta correto acima.
130:     Bc_candidates = np.abs(M_crossings_idx_B)
131:     Bc = np.median(Bc_candidates) if len(Bc_candidates) > 0 else np.nan
132: 
133:     # Mr: onde B(t) cruza zero -> le o M correspondente. Aqui x=B nao serve
134:     # como eixo de interpolacao (B passa por zero varias vezes); melhor
135:     # interpolar M em funcao do indice/tempo nos pontos onde B=0.
136:     B_crossings_idx = find_zero_crossings(np.arange(len(B)), B)
137:     if len(B_crossings_idx) > 0:
138:         M_at_Bzero = np.interp(B_crossings_idx, np.arange(len(M)), M)
139:         Mr = np.median(np.abs(M_at_Bzero))
140:     else:
141:         Mr = np.nan
142: 
143:     return Bc, Mr

150: def split_hysteresis_segments(B):
151:     """
152:     O ciclo de histerese tem 5 segmentos lineares (0->+Bmax->0->-Bmax->0->+Bmax).
153:     Detecta os pontos de inflexao (onde dB/dt muda de sinal) para dividir
154:     a serie em segmentos de rampa monotona -- avalanches sao detectadas
155:     DENTRO de cada segmento, nunca atravessando uma inflexao (onde dB/dt
156:     passa por zero e dM/dB diverge numericamente sem ser avalanche real).
157:     """
158:     dB = np.diff(B)
159:     sign_dB = np.sign(dB)
160:     sign_dB[sign_dB == 0] = 0  # pontos de B estacionario (raro, equilibrio numerico)
161:     change_idx = np.where(np.diff(sign_dB) != 0)[0] + 1
162:     bounds = [0] + list(change_idx + 1) + [len(B)]
163:     bounds = sorted(set(b for b in bounds if 0 <= b <= len(B)))
164:     segments = [(bounds[i], bounds[i + 1]) for i in range(len(bounds) - 1)
165:                 if bounds[i + 1] - bounds[i] >= 5]  # ignora segmentos degenerados (<5 pontos)
166:     return segments

169: def detect_avalanches(t, B, M, mad_threshold=4.0, min_event_len=1):
170:     """
171:     Para cada segmento de rampa monotona em B, calcula dM/dB e marca como
172:     "avalanche" os pontos onde |dM/dB - mediana_local| excede
173:     mad_threshold * MAD (median absolute deviation, robusto a outliers --
174:     apropriado aqui porque a propria distribuicao de avalanches e de
175:     cauda pesada, o que inflaria um desvio-padrao comum).
176: 
177:     Eventos contiguos (passos consecutivos acima do limiar) sao agrupados
178:     em uma unica avalanche; o "tamanho" da avalanche e a soma de |dM|
179:     absorvida durante o evento (proxy para a magnetizacao revertida
180:     naquela avalanche).
181: 
182:     Retorna: array de tamanhos de avalanche (um valor por evento detectado,
183:     agregando todos os segmentos do ciclo).
184:     """
185:     segments = split_hysteresis_segments(B)
186:     sizes = []
187: 
188:     for (i0, i1) in segments:
189:         Bs = B[i0:i1]
190:         Ms = M[i0:i1]
191:         dB_seg = np.diff(Bs)
192:         dM_seg = np.diff(Ms)
193:         # evita divisao por dB ~ 0 (nao deveria ocorrer dentro de um
194:         # segmento monotono valido, mas protege contra ruido numerico)
195:         valid = np.abs(dB_seg) > 1e-14
196:         if valid.sum() < 5:
197:             continue
198:         dMdB = np.full_like(dB_seg, np.nan)
199:         dMdB[valid] = dM_seg[valid] / dB_seg[valid]
200: 
201:         local = dMdB[valid]
202:         med = np.median(local)
203:         mad = np.median(np.abs(local - med)) + 1e-300  # evita MAD=0 exato
204:         excess = np.zeros_like(dMdB)
205:         excess[valid] = np.abs(dMdB[valid] - med) / mad
206: 
207:         is_event = excess > mad_threshold
208: 
209:         # agrupa eventos contiguos
210:         idx = np.where(is_event)[0]
211:         if len(idx) == 0:
212:             continue
213:         groups = np.split(idx, np.where(np.diff(idx) > 1)[0] + 1)
214:         for g in groups:
215:             if len(g) < min_event_len:
216:                 continue
217:             # tamanho da avalanche = soma de |dM| absorvida no evento
218:             size = np.sum(np.abs(dM_seg[g]))
219:             if size > 0:
220:                 sizes.append(size)
221: 
222:     return np.array(sizes)

229: def _mle_continuous_powerlaw(x, xmin):
230:     """
231:     Estimador de maxima verossimilhanca para o expoente tau de uma lei de
232:     potencia continua P(x) ~ x^-tau, x >= xmin (Clauset, Shalizi & Newman
233:     2009, eq. 3.1):
234: 
235:         tau_hat = 1 + n * [ sum( ln(x_i / xmin) ) ]^-1
236: 
237:     Valido para x continuo. Retorna (tau_hat, erro_padrao).
238:     """
239:     xs = x[x >= xmin]
240:     n = len(xs)
241:     if n < 10:
242:         return np.nan, np.nan, n
243:     tau_hat = 1.0 + n / np.sum(np.log(xs / xmin))
244:     sigma = (tau_hat - 1.0) / np.sqrt(n)
245:     return tau_hat, sigma, n

def rebuild_manifest_from_files(sweep_dir):
    """
    Reconstrói o dataframe de manifesto a partir dos arquivos JSON/CSV no diretório
    de sweep caso o manifest.csv original não seja encontrado.
    Compatível com saídas de damping_sweep.py, damping_sweepV02.py e sweep_damping_hysteresis.py.
    """
    import glob
    json_paths = glob.glob(os.path.join(sweep_dir, "**", "*.json"), recursive=True)
    if not json_paths:
        return None

    rows = []
    for jp in json_paths:
        try:
            with open(jp) as f:
                meta = json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            continue

        geometry = meta.get("geometry", "")
        seed = meta.get("seed", np.nan)
        damping = meta.get("damping", np.nan)
        Q = meta.get("Q", meta.get("Q_target", np.nan))
        stage = meta.get("field_mode", "")

        # Infere a etapa caso não esteja explícita
        if not stage:
            if "relax" in jp or "static" in jp:
                stage = "relax"
            else:
                stage = "hysteresis"
        elif stage == "static_relax":
            stage = "relax"

        # Tenta localizar o respectivo arquivo CSV
        base_no_ext = os.path.splitext(jp)[0]
        if base_no_ext.endswith("_hyst"):
            base_no_ext = base_no_ext[:-5]
        elif base_no_ext.endswith("_relax"):
            base_no_ext = base_no_ext[:-6]

        csv_path = base_no_ext + ".csv"
        if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
            filename = os.path.basename(csv_path)
            parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(jp))
            cand_hyst = os.path.join(parent_dir, "hysteresis", filename)
            cand_relax = os.path.join(parent_dir, "relax", filename)
            if os.path.exists(cand_hyst):
                csv_path = cand_hyst
            elif os.path.exists(cand_relax):
                csv_path = cand_relax
            else:
                continue

        tag = os.path.basename(base_no_ext)
        rows.append({
            "tag": tag,
            "stage": stage,
            "geometry": geometry,
            "seed": int(seed) if not np.isnan(seed) else seed,
            "damping": damping,
            "Q": Q,
            "csv_path": csv_path,
            "meta_path": jp,
            "n_steps": meta.get("n_steps", meta.get("n_steps_logged", np.nan)),
            "wall_seconds": meta.get("wall_seconds", meta.get("wall_time_seconds", np.nan))
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if len(df) == 0:
        return None

    # Reconstrói o damp_idx ordenando os valores únicos de Q por geometria e etapa
    df["damp_idx"] = 0
    for (geom, stg), grp in df.groupby(["geometry", "stage"]):
        unique_Qs = sorted(grp["Q"].dropna().unique(), reverse=True)
        q_to_idx = {q: idx for idx, q in enumerate(unique_Qs)}
        df.loc[grp.index, "damp_idx"] = grp["Q"].map(q_to_idx).fillna(0).astype(int)

    return df

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                  formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--sweep_dir", type=str, required=True,
                     help="Diretorio passado como --out_dir ao damping_sweep.py")
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--mad_threshold", type=float, default=4.0,
                     help="Limiar (em multiplos de MAD) para deteccao de avalanche em dM/dB")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    manifest_path = os.path.join(args.sweep_dir, "manifest.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(manifest_path):
        print(f"Aviso: manifest.csv nao encontrado em {args.sweep_dir}. Tentando reconstruir a partir dos arquivos JSON...")
        manifest = rebuild_manifest_from_files(args.sweep_dir)
        if manifest is None or len(manifest) == 0:
            print(f"ERRO: Nao foi possivel encontrar ou reconstruir o manifesto a partir dos arquivos em {args.sweep_dir}")
            sys.exit(1)
        print(f"Manifesto reconstruído com sucesso a partir de {len(manifest)} arquivos JSON/CSV.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
damping_sweep_analysis.py
==========================

Part 2 of the damping/hysteresis study: reads the results produced by
damping_sweep.py (manifest.csv + CSVs per run) and produces:

  1. For each hysteresis run: loop area, coercive field Bc, remanence Mr.
  2. Avalanche statistics: event detection in dM/dB within each ramp
     segment, and power-law fitting P(s) ~ s^-tau via maximum likelihood
     estimation (Clauset-Shalizi-Newman method), with x_min selected by
     Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) distance minimization.
  3. For each free relaxation run (Stage 2): domain size statistics (the
     domain_sizes are computed during simulation and saved in the metadata JSON).
  4. Final plots:
       - area_vs_Q.png, Bc_vs_Q.png, Mr_vs_Q.png   (one curve per geometry)
       - tau_vs_Q.png                               (the central test)
       - avalanche_histograms.png                   (P(s) per geometry for selected Q values)
       - domain_size_vs_Q.png                       (mean domain size and number vs Q)
  5. A consolidated summary_hysteresis.csv (one row per hysteresis run, containing
     all metrics), for subsequent inspection or tabulation.

Usage
-----
    python3 damping_sweep_analysis.py --sweep_dir /home/jps/sweep_results \
        --out_dir /home/jps/sweep_analysis

Dependencies: numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy.
Optional: powerlaw (if missing, uses an in-house MLE implementation equivalent
to the Clauset-Shalizi-Newman method for the continuous case, with KS-based x_min selection).
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import argparse
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

try:
    import powerlaw as _powerlaw_pkg
    _HAVE_POWERLAW = True
except ImportError:
    _HAVE_POWERLAW = False


# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Plot Styling
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.3,
    "font.size": 11,
})

GEOM_COLORS = {
    "square":     "#2E86AB",
    "triangular": "#E94560",
    "honeycomb":  "#3CB371",
}
GEOM_MARKERS = {
    "square":     "o",
    "triangular": "s",
    "honeycomb":  "^",
}


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. Hysteresis Loop Metrics: Area, Coercivity, Remanence
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def loop_area(B, M):
    """Closed hysteresis loop area via line integral
    (shoelace formula applied to the closed curve in the B-M plane).
    Equivalent to the integral of M dB over a complete cycle."""
    B = np.asarray(B)
    M = np.asarray(M)
    # Ensure the cycle is closed (last point ~ first point);
    # if not exactly closed due to numerical noise in the last step,
    # close it explicitly to prevent the line integral from leaking area.
    if not np.isclose(B[0], B[-1], atol=1e-9) or not np.isclose(M[0], M[-1], atol=1e-6):
        B = np.append(B, B[0])
        M = np.append(M, M[0])
    # Area of a closed polygon in the (B, M) plane:
    area = 0.5 * np.abs(np.sum(B[:-1] * M[1:] - B[1:] * M[:-1]))
    return area


def find_zero_crossings(x, y):
    """Returns the x values where y crosses zero, via linear interpolation
    between consecutive points of opposite signs."""
    sign = np.sign(y)
    sign[sign == 0] = 1  # Avoid false crossings at y exactly 0
    idx = np.where(np.diff(sign) != 0)[0]
    crossings = []
    for i in idx:
        x0, x1 = x[i], x[i + 1]
        y0, y1 = y[i], y[i + 1]
        if y1 == y0:
            continue
        xc = x0 + (0.0 - y0) * (x1 - x0) / (y1 - y0)
        crossings.append(xc)
    return np.array(crossings)


def coercivity_and_remanence(B, M):
    """
    Bc (coercive field)  : value of |B| where M crosses zero (average of the
                           crossings found, since the loop has more than one
                           crossing over the cycle).
    Mr (remanence)       : value of |M| where B crosses zero.
    """
    B = np.asarray(B)
    M = np.asarray(M)

    # Bc: where M(t) crosses zero -> read corresponding B
    M_crossings_idx_B = find_zero_crossings(B, M)  # x=B, y=M -> returns B where M=0
    Bc_candidates = np.abs(M_crossings_idx_B)
    Bc = np.median(Bc_candidates) if len(Bc_candidates) > 0 else np.nan

    # Mr: where B(t) crosses zero -> read corresponding M.
    # Since B passes through zero multiple times, it is better to interpolate
    # M as a function of the index/time at the points where B=0.
    B_crossings_idx = find_zero_crossings(np.arange(len(B)), B)
    if len(B_crossings_idx) > 0:
        M_at_Bzero = np.interp(B_crossings_idx, np.arange(len(M)), M)
        Mr = np.median(np.abs(M_at_Bzero))
    else:
        Mr = np.nan

    return Bc, Mr


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. Avalanche Detection via dM/dB inside Monotonic Ramps
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def split_hysteresis_segments(B):
    """
    The hysteresis cycle has 5 linear segments (0->+Bmax->0->-Bmax->0->+Bmax).
    Detects inflection points (where dB/dt changes sign) to divide the series
    into monotonic ramp segments. Avalanches are detected WITHIN each segment,
    never crossing an inflection point (where dB/dt passes through zero and
    dM/dB diverges numerically without representing a real avalanche).
    """
    dB = np.diff(B)
    sign_dB = np.sign(dB)
    sign_dB[sign_dB == 0] = 0  # Stationary B points (rare, numerical equilibrium)
    change_idx = np.where(np.diff(sign_dB) != 0)[0] + 1
    bounds = [0] + list(change_idx + 1) + [len(B)]
    bounds = sorted(set(b for b in bounds if 0 <= b <= len(B)))
    segments = [(bounds[i], bounds[i + 1]) for i in range(len(bounds) - 1)
                if bounds[i + 1] - bounds[i] >= 5]  # Ignore degenerate segments (<5 points)
    return segments


def detect_avalanches(t, B, M, mad_threshold=4.0, min_event_len=1):
    """
    For each monotonic ramp segment in B, computes dM/dB and marks as
    "avalanche" points where |dM/dB - local_median| exceeds
    mad_threshold * MAD (median absolute deviation, robust to outliers,
    which is appropriate here because the avalanche size distribution is
    heavy-tailed and would inflate a standard deviation).

    Contiguous events (consecutive steps above the threshold) are grouped
    into a single avalanche; the "size" of the avalanche is the sum of |dM|
    absorbed during the event (a proxy for the reversed magnetization).

    Returns: array of avalanche sizes (one value per detected event,
             aggregating all segments of the cycle).
    """
    segments = split_hysteresis_segments(B)
    sizes = []

    for (i0, i1) in segments:
        Bs = B[i0:i1]
        Ms = M[i0:i1]
        dB_seg = np.diff(Bs)
        dM_seg = np.diff(Ms)
        # Avoid division by dB ~ 0 (should not occur in a valid monotonic
        # segment, but protects against numerical noise)
        valid = np.abs(dB_seg) > 1e-14
        if valid.sum() < 5:
            continue
        dMdB = np.full_like(dB_seg, np.nan)
        dMdB[valid] = dM_seg[valid] / dB_seg[valid]

        local = dMdB[valid]
        med = np.median(local)
        mad = np.median(np.abs(local - med)) + 1e-300  # Avoid exact MAD=0
        excess = np.zeros_like(dMdB)
        excess[valid] = np.abs(dMdB[valid] - med) / mad

        is_event = excess > mad_threshold

        # Group contiguous events
        idx = np.where(is_event)[0]
        if len(idx) == 0:
            continue
        groups = np.split(idx, np.where(np.diff(idx) > 1)[0] + 1)
        for g in groups:
            if len(g) < min_event_len:
                continue
            # Avalanche size = sum of |dM| absorbed in the event
            size = np.sum(np.abs(dM_seg[g]))
            if size > 0:
                sizes.append(size)

    return np.array(sizes)


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3. Power-law Fitting: MLE (Clauset-Shalizi-Newman Method)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def _mle_continuous_powerlaw(x, xmin):
    """
    Maximum likelihood estimator for the power-law exponent tau of a
    continuous power law P(x) ~ x^-tau, x >= xmin (Clauset, Shalizi & Newman
    2009, eq. 3.1):

        tau_hat = 1 + n * [ sum( ln(x_i / xmin) ) ]^-1

    Valid for continuous x. Returns (tau_hat, standard_error, n).
    """
    xs = x[x >= xmin]
    n = len(xs)
    if n < 10:
        return np.nan, np.nan, n
    tau_hat = 1.0 + n / np.sum(np.log(xs / xmin))
    sigma = (tau_hat - 1.0) / np.sqrt(n)
    return tau_hat, sigma, n


def _ks_distance_powerlaw(x, xmin, tau):
    """Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the empirical CDF of x (x>=xmin)
    and the theoretical CDF of a continuous power law with exponent tau."""
    xs = np.sort(x[x >= xmin])
    n = len(xs)
    if n < 2:
        return np.inf
    cdf_emp = np.arange(1, n + 1) / n
    cdf_theo = 1.0 - (xs / xmin) ** (1.0 - tau)
    return np.max(np.abs(cdf_emp - cdf_theo))


def fit_powerlaw_mle(sizes, xmin_candidates=None):
    """
    Fits a power law to the avalanche sizes via MLE, choosing x_min by
    minimizing the KS distance (standard method from Clauset, Shalizi &
    Newman 2009 -- "Power-law distributions in empirical data").

    Uses the `powerlaw` package if available (reference implementation);
    otherwise, falls back to the in-house implementation above, which follows
    the same MLE formula and KS selection criteria.

    Returns a dict with: tau, tau_err, xmin, ks, n_tail (points in the
    fitted tail), and n_total (total points before truncation).
    """
    sizes = np.asarray(sizes)
    sizes = sizes[sizes > 0]
    n_total = len(sizes)
    if n_total < 20:
        return dict(tau=np.nan, tau_err=np.nan, xmin=np.nan, ks=np.nan,
                     n_tail=0, n_total=n_total)

    if _HAVE_POWERLAW:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            fit = _powerlaw_pkg.Fit(sizes, discrete=False, verbose=False)
        tau = fit.power_law.alpha
        tau_err = fit.power_law.sigma
        xmin = fit.power_law.xmin
        # NOTE: in some versions of the `powerlaw` package, the .KS() method is
        # broken (known bug: calls a module function without the `self.` prefix,
        # raising a NameError). The .D attribute holds the same KS distance,
        # already calculated internally during Fit() for xmin selection -- we
        # use it directly, with a fallback to .KS() in case a future version
        # removes .D.
        try:
            ks = fit.power_law.D
        except AttributeError:
            try:
                ks = fit.power_law.KS()
            except Exception:
                ks = np.nan
        n_tail = int(np.sum(sizes >= xmin))
        return dict(tau=tau, tau_err=tau_err, xmin=xmin, ks=ks,
                     n_tail=n_tail, n_total=n_total)

    # ── in-house fallback (same methodology, no external dependencies) ──
    if xmin_candidates is None:
        # candidates: quantiles of the sample (avoids testing every single point
        # when n_total is large, which would be O(n^2))
        xmin_candidates = np.unique(np.quantile(sizes, np.linspace(0.0, 0.9, 40)))
        xmin_candidates = xmin_candidates[xmin_candidates > 0]

    best = dict(tau=np.nan, tau_err=np.nan, xmin=np.nan, ks=np.inf, n_tail=0)
    for xmin in xmin_candidates:
        tau_hat, sigma, n_tail = _mle_continuous_powerlaw(sizes, xmin)
        if np.isnan(tau_hat) or n_tail < 15:
            continue
        ks = _ks_distance_powerlaw(sizes, xmin, tau_hat)
        if ks < best["ks"]:
            best = dict(tau=tau_hat, tau_err=sigma, xmin=xmin, ks=ks, n_tail=n_tail)

    best["n_total"] = n_total
    return best


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4. Main Pipeline: Parse Manifest, Process Runs, Aggregate Results
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def process_hysteresis_run(row, mad_threshold):
    df = pd.read_csv(row["csv_path"])
    B_col = "B" if "B" in df.columns else "B_proj"
    M_col = "M" if "M" in df.columns else "M_proj"
    B, M = df[B_col].values, df[M_col].values
    t = df["t"].values

    area = loop_area(B, M)
    Bc, Mr = coercivity_and_remanence(B, M)
    avalanche_sizes = detect_avalanches(t, B, M, mad_threshold=mad_threshold)

    with open(row["meta_path"]) as f:
        meta = json.load(f)

    return dict(
        tag=row["tag"], geometry=row["geometry"], damp_idx=row["damp_idx"],
        seed=row["seed"], damping=row["damping"], Q=row["Q"],
        area=area, Bc=Bc, Mr=Mr,
        n_avalanches=len(avalanche_sizes),
        avalanche_sizes=avalanche_sizes,
        B_max=meta.get("B_max", np.nan),
    )


def fit_powerlaw_per_geom_damp(summary_df):
    """
    Aggregates avalanche sizes from ALL seeds of each (geometry, damp_idx)
    combination before fitting the power law -- a single MLE fit per point
    (geometry, Q), instead of a weak fit per individual run (which typically
    has few avalanches and yields unstable/NaN tau values due to small samples).

    Returns a DataFrame with one row per (geometry, damp_idx): Q_mean,
    tau, tau_err, xmin, ks, n_tail, n_total (aggregated), and n_seeds.
    """
    rows = []
    for (geom, di), grp in summary_df.groupby(["geometry", "damp_idx"]):
        all_sizes = np.concatenate(grp["avalanche_sizes"].values) \
            if len(grp) else np.array([])
        fit = fit_powerlaw_mle(all_sizes)
        rows.append(dict(
            geometry=geom, damp_idx=di, Q_mean=grp["Q"].mean(),
            tau=fit["tau"], tau_err=fit["tau_err"], xmin=fit["xmin"],
            ks=fit["ks"], n_tail=fit["n_tail"], n_total=fit.get("n_total", 0),
            n_seeds=len(grp),
        ))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["geometry", "damp_idx"])


def process_relax_run(row):
    with open(row["meta_path"]) as f:
        meta = json.load(f)
    sizes = np.array(meta.get("domain_sizes", []))
    sizes = sizes[sizes > 0]
    if len(sizes) == 0:
        mean_size, max_size, n_dom = np.nan, np.nan, 0
    else:
        mean_size = float(np.mean(sizes))
        max_size = float(np.max(sizes))
        n_dom = len(sizes)
    return dict(
        tag=row["tag"], geometry=row["geometry"], damp_idx=row["damp_idx"],
        seed=row["seed"], damping=row["damping"], Q=row["Q"],
        n_domains=n_dom, mean_domain_size=mean_size, max_domain_size=max_size,
    )


def aggregate_by_geom_damp(df, value_cols):
    """Aggregates (mean, standard deviation) over seeds for each (geometry, damp_idx),
    preserving Q (which is approximately constant across seeds, since it only depends on
    geometry/damping/r_nn -- minor variations of r_nn between geometries are expected
    and the Q of each individual run is already recorded; here we average Q for consistency)."""
    agg_funcs = {c: ["mean", "std"] for c in value_cols}
    agg_funcs["Q"] = ["mean"]
    g = df.groupby(["geometry", "damp_idx"]).agg(agg_funcs)
    g.columns = ["_".join(c) for c in g.columns]
    g = g.reset_index().sort_values(["geometry", "damp_idx"])
    return g


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5. Plots
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_df, value_col, ylabel, title, out_path, logy=False):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
    for geom in agg_df["geometry"].unique():
        sub = agg_df[agg_df["geometry"] == geom].sort_values("Q_mean")
        ax.errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub[f"{value_col}_mean"],
                     yerr=sub[f"{value_col}_std"],
                     marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                     color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                     label=geom, capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=6)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    if logy:
        ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$Q = \omega_0 I / b$  (quality factor)")
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.legend(title="Geometry")
    ax.axvline(1.0, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
    ax.text(1.0, ax.get_ylim()[1], "  Q=1\n  (crossover)", fontsize=8,
            color="gray", va="top")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def plot_avalanche_histograms(summary_df, out_path, n_Q_examples=3):
    """For each geometry, plots P(s) in log-log for representative Q values
    (underdamped, crossover, overdamped) with the fitted MLE line overlaid."""
    geometries = sorted(summary_df["geometry"].unique())
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(geometries), figsize=(5.5 * len(geometries), 5),
                              sharey=True)
    if len(geometries) == 1:
        axes = [axes]

    for ax, geom in zip(axes, geometries):
        sub = summary_df[summary_df["geometry"] == geom]
        damp_idxs = sorted(sub["damp_idx"].unique())
        chosen = [damp_idxs[0], damp_idxs[len(damp_idxs) // 2], damp_idxs[-1]] \
            if len(damp_idxs) >= 3 else damp_idxs

        for di in chosen:
            rows = sub[sub["damp_idx"] == di]
            all_sizes = np.concatenate(rows["avalanche_sizes"].values) \
                if len(rows) else np.array([])
            all_sizes = all_sizes[all_sizes > 0]
            Q_label = rows["Q"].mean()
            if len(all_sizes) < 20:
                ax.plot([], [], " ", label=f"Q≈{Q_label:.2f}  (n={len(all_sizes)}, "
                                             f"insufficient for fit)")
                continue

            # log-binned histogram (for visualization only -- the tau fit
            # shown in other plots comes directly from MLE, not from this histogram)
            if all_sizes.min() == all_sizes.max():
                bins = np.linspace(all_sizes.min() * 0.9, all_sizes.max() * 1.1, 25)
            else:
                bins = np.geomspace(all_sizes.min(), all_sizes.max(), 25)
            hist, edges = np.histogram(all_sizes, bins=bins, density=True)
            centers = np.sqrt(edges[:-1] * edges[1:])
            mask = hist > 0
            pts = ax.loglog(centers[mask], hist[mask], "o", ms=4,
                             label=f"Q≈{Q_label:.2f}  (n={len(all_sizes)})")
            color = pts[0].get_color()

            fit = fit_powerlaw_mle(all_sizes)
            if not np.isnan(fit["tau"]):
                if fit["xmin"] == all_sizes.max():
                    xs_line = np.linspace(fit["xmin"] * 0.9, all_sizes.max() * 1.1, 50)
                else:
                    xs_line = np.geomspace(fit["xmin"], all_sizes.max(), 50)
                ys_line = (fit["tau"] - 1.0) / fit["xmin"] * (xs_line / fit["xmin"]) ** (-fit["tau"])
                # anchor the MLE line to the histogram point nearest to xmin
                # (instead of the last bin) where the fit actually starts --
                # prevents visual misalignment of the line when the tail has few bins.
                idx_anchor = np.argmin(np.abs(centers[mask] - fit["xmin"]))
                anchor_hist_y = hist[mask][idx_anchor]
                anchor_line_y = (fit["tau"] - 1.0) / fit["xmin"] * \
                    (centers[mask][idx_anchor] / fit["xmin"]) ** (-fit["tau"])
                scale = anchor_hist_y / (anchor_line_y + 1e-300)
                ax.loglog(xs_line, ys_line * scale, "--", lw=1.2,
                           color=color, alpha=0.7,
                           label=f"  MLE: τ={fit['tau']:.2f}±{fit['tau_err']:.2f}")

        ax.set_title(f"{geom}")
        ax.set_xlabel("avalanche size $s$")
        if ax is axes[0]:
            ax.set_ylabel(r"$P(s)$")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)

    fig.suptitle("Avalanche size distributions (dots: log-binned histogram; "
                  "dashed line: tail MLE fit)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def plot_tau_vs_Q(tau_df, out_path):
    """The central plot of the study: tau (avalanche power-law exponent) as a
    function of Q, by geometry. The fit of tau uses ALL seeds aggregated for each
    (geometry, damp_idx) -- see fit_powerlaw_per_geom_damp -- yielding a single point
    (with MLE error bars) per geometry/Q instead of a weak fit per individual run.

    A flat curve (tau ~ const) supports the 'incremental' result; a systematic
    variation of tau with Q, or qualitative differences between geometries, represents
    the 'surprising' signature of universality class dependence under long-range,
    anisotropic dipolar coupling."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.5))
    for geom in tau_df["geometry"].unique():
        sub = tau_df[tau_df["geometry"] == geom].dropna(subset=["tau"]).sort_values("Q_mean")
        if len(sub) == 0:
            continue
        ax.errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub["tau"], yerr=sub["tau_err"],
                     marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                     color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                     label=f"{geom}  (mean n_tail={sub['n_tail'].mean():.0f})",
                     capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=7)

    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$Q = \omega_0 I / b$  (quality factor)")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"power-law exponent $\tau$  [$P(s) \sim s^{-\tau}$]")
    ax.set_title("Central test: avalanche exponent vs. quality factor\n"
                  "(avalanches aggregated across seeds before MLE fit)")
    ax.axvline(1.0, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
    ax.legend(title="Geometry", fontsize=9)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def plot_domain_stats_vs_Q(relax_df, out_path):
    agg = aggregate_by_geom_damp(relax_df, ["mean_domain_size", "n_domains"])

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
    for geom in agg["geometry"].unique():
        sub = agg[agg["geometry"] == geom].sort_values("Q_mean")
        axes[0].errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub["mean_domain_size_mean"],
                          yerr=sub["mean_domain_size_std"],
                          marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                          color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                          label=geom, capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=6)
        axes[1].errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub["n_domains_mean"],
                          yerr=sub["n_domains_std"],
                          marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                          color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                          label=geom, capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=6)

    for ax, ylabel, title in zip(
            axes,
            ["mean domain size (no. of needles)", "number of domains"],
            ["Mean domain size vs. Q", "Number of domains vs. Q"]):
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xlabel(r"$Q = \omega_0 I / b$")
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.axvline(1.0, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
        ax.legend(title="Geometry")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def rebuild_manifest_from_files(sweep_dir):
    """
    Rebuilds the manifest DataFrame from the JSON/CSV files in the sweep directory
    when manifest.csv is missing.
    Compatible with outputs from damping_sweep.py, damping_sweepV02.py, and sweep_damping_hysteresis.py.
    """
    import glob
    json_paths = glob.glob(os.path.join(sweep_dir, "**", "*.json"), recursive=True)
    if not json_paths:
        return None

    rows = []
    for jp in json_paths:
        try:
            with open(jp) as f:
                meta = json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            continue

        geometry = meta.get("geometry", "")
        seed = meta.get("seed", np.nan)
        damping = meta.get("damping", np.nan)
        Q = meta.get("Q", meta.get("Q_target", np.nan))
        stage = meta.get("field_mode", "")

        # Infer stage if not explicit
        if not stage:
            if "relax" in jp or "static" in jp:
                stage = "relax"
            else:
                stage = "hysteresis"
        elif stage == "static_relax":
            stage = "relax"

        # Try to locate the respective CSV file
        base_no_ext = os.path.splitext(jp)[0]
        if base_no_ext.endswith("_hyst"):
            base_no_ext = base_no_ext[:-5]
        elif base_no_ext.endswith("_relax"):
            base_no_ext = base_no_ext[:-6]

        csv_path = base_no_ext + ".csv"
        if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
            filename = os.path.basename(csv_path)
            parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(jp))
            cand_hyst = os.path.join(parent_dir, "hysteresis", filename)
            cand_relax = os.path.join(parent_dir, "relax", filename)
            if os.path.exists(cand_hyst):
                csv_path = cand_hyst
            elif os.path.exists(cand_relax):
                csv_path = cand_relax
            else:
                continue

        tag = os.path.basename(base_no_ext)
        rows.append({
            "tag": tag,
            "stage": stage,
            "geometry": geometry,
            "seed": int(seed) if not np.isnan(seed) else seed,
            "damping": damping,
            "Q": Q,
            "csv_path": csv_path,
            "meta_path": jp,
            "n_steps": meta.get("n_steps", meta.get("n_steps_logged", np.nan)),
            "wall_seconds": meta.get("wall_seconds", meta.get("wall_time_seconds", np.nan))
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if len(df) == 0:
        return None

    # Reconstruct damp_idx by sorting the unique values of Q per geometry and stage
    df["damp_idx"] = 0
    for (geom, stg), grp in df.groupby(["geometry", "stage"]):
        unique_Qs = sorted(grp["Q"].dropna().unique(), reverse=True)
        q_to_idx = {q: idx for idx, q in enumerate(unique_Qs)}
        df.loc[grp.index, "damp_idx"] = grp["Q"].map(q_to_idx).fillna(0).astype(int)

    return df


# main
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                  formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--sweep_dir", type=str, required=True,
                     help="Directory passed as --out_dir to damping_sweep.py")
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--mad_threshold", type=float, default=4.0,
                     help="Threshold (in multiples of MAD) for avalanche detection in dM/dB")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    manifest_path = os.path.join(args.sweep_dir, "manifest.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(manifest_path):
        print(f"Warning: manifest.csv not found in {args.sweep_dir}. Attempting to rebuild from JSON files...")
        manifest = rebuild_manifest_from_files(args.sweep_dir)
        if manifest is None or len(manifest) == 0:
            print(f"ERROR: Could not find or reconstruct manifest from files in {args.sweep_dir}")
            sys.exit(1)
        print(f"Manifest successfully reconstructed from {len(manifest)} JSON/CSV files.")
    else:
        manifest = pd.read_csv(manifest_path)

    hyst_rows = manifest[manifest["stage"] == "hysteresis"]
    relax_rows = manifest[manifest["stage"] == "relax"]

    print(f"Manifest: {len(hyst_rows)} hysteresis runs, "
          f"{len(relax_rows)} relaxation runs.")

    summary_df = pd.DataFrame()
    relax_df = pd.DataFrame()

    # ── Stage 1: process each hysteresis run ──────────────────────
    if len(hyst_rows) > 0:
        print("\nProcessing hysteresis runs (area, Bc, Mr, avalanches, MLE)...")
        hyst_results = []
        for i, (_, row) in enumerate(hyst_rows.iterrows()):
            print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(hyst_rows)}] {row['tag']}", end="\r")
            hyst_results.append(process_hysteresis_run(row, args.mad_threshold))
        print()

        summary_df = pd.DataFrame(hyst_results)
        if "avalanche_sizes" in summary_df.columns:
            summary_csv = summary_df.drop(columns=["avalanche_sizes"])
        else:
            summary_csv = summary_df
        summary_csv_path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, "summary_hysteresis.csv")
        summary_csv.to_csv(summary_csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Saved: {summary_csv_path}")

        # ── power-law fitting: aggregates avalanches across seeds BEFORE
        #    running MLE for each (geometry, damp_idx) point -- see function docstring.
        print("\nFitting power law (avalanches aggregated across seeds)...")
        tau_df = fit_powerlaw_per_geom_damp(summary_df)
        tau_csv_path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, "powerlaw_fits.csv")
        tau_df.to_csv(tau_csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Saved: {tau_csv_path}")
        print(tau_df.to_string(index=False))

        # ── aggregates (mean+std across seeds) of loop metrics ──────────
        print("\nGenerating hysteresis plots...")
        agg_loop = aggregate_by_geom_damp(summary_df, ["area", "Bc", "Mr"])
        agg_loop.to_csv(os.path.join(args.out_dir, "aggregated_loop_metrics.csv"), index=False)

        plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_loop, "area", "hysteresis loop area  [T]",
                          "Loop area vs. quality factor",
                          os.path.join(args.out_dir, "area_vs_Q.png"))
        plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_loop, "Bc", r"coercive field $B_c$  [T]",
                          "Coercive field vs. quality factor",
                          os.path.join(args.out_dir, "Bc_vs_Q.png"))
        plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_loop, "Mr", r"remanence $M_r$",
                          "Remanence vs. quality factor",
                          os.path.join(args.out_dir, "Mr_vs_Q.png"))

        # ── central plot: tau(Q) ─────────────────────────────────────
        plot_tau_vs_Q(tau_df, os.path.join(args.out_dir, "tau_vs_Q.png"))

        # ── avalanche histograms (visual, selected geometries/Q) ─────────
        plot_avalanche_histograms(summary_df, os.path.join(args.out_dir, "avalanche_histograms.png"))
    else:
        print("\nNo hysteresis runs found.")

    # ── Stage 2: process each relaxation run ───────────────────────
    if len(relax_rows) > 0:
        print("\nProcessing relaxation runs (domain statistics)...")
        relax_results = [process_relax_run(row) for _, row in relax_rows.iterrows()]
        relax_df = pd.DataFrame(relax_results)
        relax_csv_path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, "summary_relax.csv")
        relax_df.to_csv(relax_csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Saved: {relax_csv_path}")

        # ── domains vs Q ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        plot_domain_stats_vs_Q(relax_df, os.path.join(args.out_dir, "domain_size_vs_Q.png"))
    else:
        print("\nNo relaxation runs found.")

    print(f"\nCompleted. Results in: {args.out_dir}")
    print("Generated files:")
    files_to_print = []
    if not summary_df.empty:
        files_to_print += ["summary_hysteresis.csv", "aggregated_loop_metrics.csv", "powerlaw_fits.csv",
                           "area_vs_Q.png", "Bc_vs_Q.png", "Mr_vs_Q.png", "tau_vs_Q.png", "avalanche_histograms.png"]
    if not relax_df.empty:
        files_to_print += ["summary_relax.csv", "domain_size_vs_Q.png"]
    for fname in files_to_print:
        print(f"  - {fname}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
damping_sweep_analysis.py
==========================

Part 2 of the damping/hysteresis study: reads the results produced by
damping_sweep.py (manifest.csv + CSVs per run) and produces:

  1. For each hysteresis run: loop area, coercive field Bc, remanence Mr.
  2. Avalanche statistics: event detection in dM/dB within each ramp
     segment, and power-law fitting P(s) ~ s^-tau via maximum likelihood
     estimation (Clauset-Shalizi-Newman method), with x_min selected by
     Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) distance minimization.
  3. For each free relaxation run (Stage 2): domain size statistics (the
     domain_sizes are computed during simulation and saved in the metadata JSON).
  4. Final plots:
       - area_vs_Q.png, Bc_vs_Q.png, Mr_vs_Q.png   (one curve per geometry)
       - tau_vs_Q.png                               (the central test)
       - avalanche_histograms.png                   (P(s) per geometry for selected Q values)
       - domain_size_vs_Q.png                       (mean domain size and number vs Q)
  5. A consolidated summary_hysteresis.csv (one row per hysteresis run, containing
     all metrics), for subsequent inspection or tabulation.

Usage
-----
    python3 damping_sweep_analysis.py --sweep_dir /home/jps/sweep_results \
        --out_dir /home/jps/sweep_analysis

Dependencies: numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy.
Optional: powerlaw (if missing, uses an in-house MLE implementation equivalent
to the Clauset-Shalizi-Newman method for the continuous case, with KS-based x_min selection).
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import argparse
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

try:
    import powerlaw as _powerlaw_pkg
    _HAVE_POWERLAW = True
except ImportError:
    _HAVE_POWERLAW = False


# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Plot Styling
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.3,
    "font.size": 11,
})

GEOM_COLORS = {
    "square":     "#2E86AB",
    "triangular": "#E94560",
    "honeycomb":  "#3CB371",
}
GEOM_MARKERS = {
    "square":     "o",
    "triangular": "s",
    "honeycomb":  "^",
}


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. Hysteresis Loop Metrics: Area, Coercivity, Remanence
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def loop_area(B, M):
    """Closed hysteresis loop area via line integral
    (shoelace formula applied to the closed curve in the B-M plane).
    Equivalent to the integral of M dB over a complete cycle."""
    B = np.asarray(B)
    M = np.asarray(M)
    # Ensure the cycle is closed (last point ~ first point);
    # if not exactly closed due to numerical noise in the last step,
    # close it explicitly to prevent the line integral from leaking area.
    if not np.isclose(B[0], B[-1], atol=1e-9) or not np.isclose(M[0], M[-1], atol=1e-6):
        B = np.append(B, B[0])
        M = np.append(M, M[0])
    # Area of a closed polygon in the (B, M) plane:
    area = 0.5 * np.abs(np.sum(B[:-1] * M[1:] - B[1:] * M[:-1]))
    return area


def find_zero_crossings(x, y):
    """Returns the x values where y crosses zero, via linear interpolation
    between consecutive points of opposite signs."""
    sign = np.sign(y)
    sign[sign == 0] = 1  # Avoid false crossings at y exactly 0
    idx = np.where(np.diff(sign) != 0)[0]
    crossings = []
    for i in idx:
        x0, x1 = x[i], x[i + 1]
        y0, y1 = y[i], y[i + 1]
        if y1 == y0:
            continue
        xc = x0 + (0.0 - y0) * (x1 - x0) / (y1 - y0)
        crossings.append(xc)
    return np.array(crossings)


def coercivity_and_remanence(B, M):
    """
    Bc (coercive field)  : value of |B| where M crosses zero (average of the
                           crossings found, since the loop has more than one
                           crossing over the cycle).
    Mr (remanence)       : value of |M| where B crosses zero.
    """
    B = np.asarray(B)
    M = np.asarray(M)

    # Bc: where M(t) crosses zero -> read corresponding B
    M_crossings_idx_B = find_zero_crossings(B, M)  # x=B, y=M -> returns B where M=0
    Bc_candidates = np.abs(M_crossings_idx_B)
    Bc = np.median(Bc_candidates) if len(Bc_candidates) > 0 else np.nan

    # Mr: where B(t) crosses zero -> read corresponding M.
    # Since B passes through zero multiple times, it is better to interpolate
    # M as a function of the index/time at the points where B=0.
    B_crossings_idx = find_zero_crossings(np.arange(len(B)), B)
    if len(B_crossings_idx) > 0:
        M_at_Bzero = np.interp(B_crossings_idx, np.arange(len(M)), M)
        Mr = np.median(np.abs(M_at_Bzero))
    else:
        Mr = np.nan

    return Bc, Mr


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2. Avalanche Detection via dM/dB inside Monotonic Ramps
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def split_hysteresis_segments(B):
    """
    The hysteresis cycle has 5 linear segments (0->+Bmax->0->-Bmax->0->+Bmax).
    Detects inflection points (where dB/dt changes sign) to divide the series
    into monotonic ramp segments. Avalanches are detected WITHIN each segment,
    never crossing an inflection point (where dB/dt passes through zero and
    dM/dB diverges numerically without representing a real avalanche).
    """
    dB = np.diff(B)
    sign_dB = np.sign(dB)
    sign_dB[sign_dB == 0] = 0  # Stationary B points (rare, numerical equilibrium)
    change_idx = np.where(np.diff(sign_dB) != 0)[0] + 1
    bounds = [0] + list(change_idx + 1) + [len(B)]
    bounds = sorted(set(b for b in bounds if 0 <= b <= len(B)))
    segments = [(bounds[i], bounds[i + 1]) for i in range(len(bounds) - 1)
                if bounds[i + 1] - bounds[i] >= 5]  # Ignore degenerate segments (<5 points)
    return segments


def detect_avalanches(t, B, M, mad_threshold=4.0, min_event_len=1):
    """
    For each monotonic ramp segment in B, computes dM/dB and marks as
    "avalanche" points where |dM/dB - local_median| exceeds
    mad_threshold * MAD (median absolute deviation, robust to outliers,
    which is appropriate here because the avalanche size distribution is
    heavy-tailed and would inflate a standard deviation).

    Contiguous events (consecutive steps above the threshold) are grouped
    into a single avalanche; the "size" of the avalanche is the sum of |dM|
    absorbed during the event (a proxy for the reversed magnetization).

    Returns: array of avalanche sizes (one value per detected event,
             aggregating all segments of the cycle).
    """
    segments = split_hysteresis_segments(B)
    sizes = []

    for (i0, i1) in segments:
        Bs = B[i0:i1]
        Ms = M[i0:i1]
        dB_seg = np.diff(Bs)
        dM_seg = np.diff(Ms)
        # Avoid division by dB ~ 0 (should not occur in a valid monotonic
        # segment, but protects against numerical noise)
        valid = np.abs(dB_seg) > 1e-14
        if valid.sum() < 5:
            continue
        dMdB = np.full_like(dB_seg, np.nan)
        dMdB[valid] = dM_seg[valid] / dB_seg[valid]

        local = dMdB[valid]
        med = np.median(local)
        mad = np.median(np.abs(local - med)) + 1e-300  # Avoid exact MAD=0
        excess = np.zeros_like(dMdB)
        excess[valid] = np.abs(dMdB[valid] - med) / mad

        is_event = excess > mad_threshold

        # Group contiguous events
        idx = np.where(is_event)[0]
        if len(idx) == 0:
            continue
        groups = np.split(idx, np.where(np.diff(idx) > 1)[0] + 1)
        for g in groups:
            if len(g) < min_event_len:
                continue
            # Avalanche size = sum of |dM| absorbed in the event
            size = np.sum(np.abs(dM_seg[g]))
            if size > 0:
                sizes.append(size)

    return np.array(sizes)


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3. Power-law Fitting: MLE (Clauset-Shalizi-Newman Method)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def _mle_continuous_powerlaw(x, xmin):
    """
    Maximum likelihood estimator for the power-law exponent tau of a
    continuous power law P(x) ~ x^-tau, x >= xmin (Clauset, Shalizi & Newman
    2009, eq. 3.1):

        tau_hat = 1 + n * [ sum( ln(x_i / xmin) ) ]^-1

    Valid for continuous x. Returns (tau_hat, standard_error, n).
    """
    xs = x[x >= xmin]
    n = len(xs)
    if n < 10:
        return np.nan, np.nan, n
    tau_hat = 1.0 + n / np.sum(np.log(xs / xmin))
    sigma = (tau_hat - 1.0) / np.sqrt(n)
    return tau_hat, sigma, n


def _ks_distance_powerlaw(x, xmin, tau):
    """Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the empirical CDF of x (x>=xmin)
    and the theoretical CDF of a continuous power law with exponent tau."""
    xs = np.sort(x[x >= xmin])
    n = len(xs)
    if n < 2:
        return np.inf
    cdf_emp = np.arange(1, n + 1) / n
    cdf_theo = 1.0 - (xs / xmin) ** (1.0 - tau)
    return np.max(np.abs(cdf_emp - cdf_theo))


def fit_powerlaw_mle(sizes, xmin_candidates=None):
    """
    Fits a power law to the avalanche sizes via MLE, choosing x_min by
    minimizing the KS distance (standard method from Clauset, Shalizi &
    Newman 2009 -- "Power-law distributions in empirical data").

    Uses the `powerlaw` package if available (reference implementation);
    otherwise, falls back to the in-house implementation above, which follows
    the same MLE formula and KS selection criteria.

    Returns a dict with: tau, tau_err, xmin, ks, n_tail (points in the
    fitted tail), and n_total (total points before truncation).
    """
    sizes = np.asarray(sizes)
    sizes = sizes[sizes > 0]
    n_total = len(sizes)
    if n_total < 20:
        return dict(tau=np.nan, tau_err=np.nan, xmin=np.nan, ks=np.nan,
                     n_tail=0, n_total=n_total)

    if _HAVE_POWERLAW:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            fit = _powerlaw_pkg.Fit(sizes, discrete=False, verbose=False)
        tau = fit.power_law.alpha
        tau_err = fit.power_law.sigma
        xmin = fit.power_law.xmin
        # NOTE: in some versions of the `powerlaw` package, the .KS() method is
        # broken (known bug: calls a module function without the `self.` prefix,
        # raising a NameError). The .D attribute holds the same KS distance,
        # already calculated internally during Fit() for xmin selection -- we
        # use it directly, with a fallback to .KS() in case a future version
        # removes .D.
        try:
            ks = fit.power_law.D
        except AttributeError:
            try:
                ks = fit.power_law.KS()
            except Exception:
                ks = np.nan
        n_tail = int(np.sum(sizes >= xmin))
        return dict(tau=tau, tau_err=tau_err, xmin=xmin, ks=ks,
                     n_tail=n_tail, n_total=n_total)

    # ── in-house fallback (same methodology, no external dependencies) ──
    if xmin_candidates is None:
        # candidates: quantiles of the sample (avoids testing every single point
        # when n_total is large, which would be O(n^2))
        xmin_candidates = np.unique(np.quantile(sizes, np.linspace(0.0, 0.9, 40)))
        xmin_candidates = xmin_candidates[xmin_candidates > 0]

    best = dict(tau=np.nan, tau_err=np.nan, xmin=np.nan, ks=np.inf, n_tail=0)
    for xmin in xmin_candidates:
        tau_hat, sigma, n_tail = _mle_continuous_powerlaw(sizes, xmin)
        if np.isnan(tau_hat) or n_tail < 15:
            continue
        ks = _ks_distance_powerlaw(sizes, xmin, tau_hat)
        if ks < best["ks"]:
            best = dict(tau=tau_hat, tau_err=sigma, xmin=xmin, ks=ks, n_tail=n_tail)

    best["n_total"] = n_total
    return best


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4. Main Pipeline: Parse Manifest, Process Runs, Aggregate Results
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def process_hysteresis_run(row, mad_threshold):
    df = pd.read_csv(row["csv_path"])
    B_col = "B" if "B" in df.columns else "B_proj"
    M_col = "M" if "M" in df.columns else "M_proj"
    B, M = df[B_col].values, df[M_col].values
    t = df["t"].values

    area = loop_area(B, M)
    Bc, Mr = coercivity_and_remanence(B, M)
    avalanche_sizes = detect_avalanches(t, B, M, mad_threshold=mad_threshold)

    with open(row["meta_path"]) as f:
        meta = json.load(f)

    return dict(
        tag=row["tag"], geometry=row["geometry"], damp_idx=row["damp_idx"],
        seed=row["seed"], damping=row["damping"], Q=row["Q"],
        area=area, Bc=Bc, Mr=Mr,
        n_avalanches=len(avalanche_sizes),
        avalanche_sizes=avalanche_sizes,
        B_max=meta.get("B_max", np.nan),
    )


def fit_powerlaw_per_geom_damp(summary_df):
    """
    Aggregates avalanche sizes from ALL seeds of each (geometry, damp_idx)
    combination before fitting the power law -- a single MLE fit per point
    (geometry, Q), instead of a weak fit per individual run (which typically
    has few avalanches and yields unstable/NaN tau values due to small samples).

    Returns a DataFrame with one row per (geometry, damp_idx): Q_mean,
    tau, tau_err, xmin, ks, n_tail, n_total (aggregated), and n_seeds.
    """
    rows = []
    for (geom, di), grp in summary_df.groupby(["geometry", "damp_idx"]):
        all_sizes = np.concatenate(grp["avalanche_sizes"].values) \
            if len(grp) else np.array([])
        fit = fit_powerlaw_mle(all_sizes)
        rows.append(dict(
            geometry=geom, damp_idx=di, Q_mean=grp["Q"].mean(),
            tau=fit["tau"], tau_err=fit["tau_err"], xmin=fit["xmin"],
            ks=fit["ks"], n_tail=fit["n_tail"], n_total=fit.get("n_total", 0),
            n_seeds=len(grp),
        ))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["geometry", "damp_idx"])


def process_relax_run(row):
    with open(row["meta_path"]) as f:
        meta = json.load(f)
    sizes = np.array(meta.get("domain_sizes", []))
    sizes = sizes[sizes > 0]
    if len(sizes) == 0:
        mean_size, max_size, n_dom = np.nan, np.nan, 0
    else:
        mean_size = float(np.mean(sizes))
        max_size = float(np.max(sizes))
        n_dom = len(sizes)
    return dict(
        tag=row["tag"], geometry=row["geometry"], damp_idx=row["damp_idx"],
        seed=row["seed"], damping=row["damping"], Q=row["Q"],
        n_domains=n_dom, mean_domain_size=mean_size, max_domain_size=max_size,
    )


def aggregate_by_geom_damp(df, value_cols):
    """Aggregates (mean, standard deviation) over seeds for each (geometry, damp_idx),
    preserving Q (which is approximately constant across seeds, since it only depends on
    geometry/damping/r_nn -- minor variations of r_nn between geometries are expected
    and the Q of each individual run is already recorded; here we average Q for consistency)."""
    agg_funcs = {c: ["mean", "std"] for c in value_cols}
    agg_funcs["Q"] = ["mean"]
    g = df.groupby(["geometry", "damp_idx"]).agg(agg_funcs)
    g.columns = ["_".join(c) for c in g.columns]
    g = g.reset_index().sort_values(["geometry", "damp_idx"])
    return g


# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5. Plots
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_df, value_col, ylabel, title, out_path, logy=False):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
    for geom in agg_df["geometry"].unique():
        sub = agg_df[agg_df["geometry"] == geom].sort_values("Q_mean")
        ax.errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub[f"{value_col}_mean"],
                     yerr=sub[f"{value_col}_std"],
                     marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                     color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                     label=geom, capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=6)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    if logy:
        ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$Q = \omega_0 I / b$  (quality factor)")
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.legend(title="Geometry")
    ax.axvline(1.0, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
    ax.text(1.0, ax.get_ylim()[1], "  Q=1\n  (crossover)", fontsize=8,
            color="gray", va="top")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def plot_avalanche_histograms(summary_df, out_path, n_Q_examples=3):
    """For each geometry, plots P(s) in log-log for representative Q values
    (underdamped, crossover, overdamped) with the fitted MLE line overlaid."""
    geometries = sorted(summary_df["geometry"].unique())
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(geometries), figsize=(5.5 * len(geometries), 5),
                              sharey=True)
    if len(geometries) == 1:
        axes = [axes]

    for ax, geom in zip(axes, geometries):
        sub = summary_df[summary_df["geometry"] == geom]
        damp_idxs = sorted(sub["damp_idx"].unique())
        chosen = [damp_idxs[0], damp_idxs[len(damp_idxs) // 2], damp_idxs[-1]] \
            if len(damp_idxs) >= 3 else damp_idxs

        for di in chosen:
            rows = sub[sub["damp_idx"] == di]
            all_sizes = np.concatenate(rows["avalanche_sizes"].values) \
                if len(rows) else np.array([])
            all_sizes = all_sizes[all_sizes > 0]
            Q_label = rows["Q"].mean()
            if len(all_sizes) < 20:
                ax.plot([], [], " ", label=f"Q≈{Q_label:.2f}  (n={len(all_sizes)}, "
                                             f"insufficient for fit)")
                continue

            # log-binned histogram (for visualization only -- the tau fit
            # shown in other plots comes directly from MLE, not from this histogram)
            if all_sizes.min() == all_sizes.max():
                bins = np.linspace(all_sizes.min() * 0.9, all_sizes.max() * 1.1, 25)
            else:
                bins = np.geomspace(all_sizes.min(), all_sizes.max(), 25)
            hist, edges = np.histogram(all_sizes, bins=bins, density=True)
            centers = np.sqrt(edges[:-1] * edges[1:])
            mask = hist > 0
            pts = ax.loglog(centers[mask], hist[mask], "o", ms=4,
                             label=f"Q≈{Q_label:.2f}  (n={len(all_sizes)})")
            color = pts[0].get_color()

            fit = fit_powerlaw_mle(all_sizes)
            if not np.isnan(fit["tau"]):
                if fit["xmin"] == all_sizes.max():
                    xs_line = np.linspace(fit["xmin"] * 0.9, all_sizes.max() * 1.1, 50)
                else:
                    xs_line = np.geomspace(fit["xmin"], all_sizes.max(), 50)
                ys_line = (fit["tau"] - 1.0) / fit["xmin"] * (xs_line / fit["xmin"]) ** (-fit["tau"])
                # anchor the MLE line to the histogram point nearest to xmin
                # (instead of the last bin) where the fit actually starts --
                # prevents visual misalignment of the line when the tail has few bins.
                idx_anchor = np.argmin(np.abs(centers[mask] - fit["xmin"]))
                anchor_hist_y = hist[mask][idx_anchor]
                anchor_line_y = (fit["tau"] - 1.0) / fit["xmin"] * \
                    (centers[mask][idx_anchor] / fit["xmin"]) ** (-fit["tau"])
                scale = anchor_hist_y / (anchor_line_y + 1e-300)
                ax.loglog(xs_line, ys_line * scale, "--", lw=1.2,
                           color=color, alpha=0.7,
                           label=f"  MLE: τ={fit['tau']:.2f}±{fit['tau_err']:.2f}")

        ax.set_title(f"{geom}")
        ax.set_xlabel("avalanche size $s$")
        if ax is axes[0]:
            ax.set_ylabel(r"$P(s)$")
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)

    fig.suptitle("Avalanche size distributions (dots: log-binned histogram; "
                  "dashed line: tail MLE fit)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def plot_tau_vs_Q(tau_df, out_path):
    """The central plot of the study: tau (avalanche power-law exponent) as a
    function of Q, by geometry. The fit of tau uses ALL seeds aggregated for each
    (geometry, damp_idx) -- see fit_powerlaw_per_geom_damp -- yielding a single point
    (with MLE error bars) per geometry/Q instead of a weak fit per individual run.

    A flat curve (tau ~ const) supports the 'incremental' result; a systematic
    variation of tau with Q, or qualitative differences between geometries, represents
    the 'surprising' signature of universality class dependence under long-range,
    anisotropic dipolar coupling."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.5))
    for geom in tau_df["geometry"].unique():
        sub = tau_df[tau_df["geometry"] == geom].dropna(subset=["tau"]).sort_values("Q_mean")
        if len(sub) == 0:
            continue
        ax.errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub["tau"], yerr=sub["tau_err"],
                     marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                     color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                     label=f"{geom}  (mean n_tail={sub['n_tail'].mean():.0f})",
                     capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=7)

    ax.set_xscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$Q = \omega_0 I / b$  (quality factor)")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"power-law exponent $\tau$  [$P(s) \sim s^{-\tau}$]")
    ax.set_title("Central test: avalanche exponent vs. quality factor\n"
                  "(avalanches aggregated across seeds before MLE fit)")
    ax.axvline(1.0, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
    ax.legend(title="Geometry", fontsize=9)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def plot_domain_stats_vs_Q(relax_df, out_path):
    agg = aggregate_by_geom_damp(relax_df, ["mean_domain_size", "n_domains"])

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
    for geom in agg["geometry"].unique():
        sub = agg[agg["geometry"] == geom].sort_values("Q_mean")
        axes[0].errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub["mean_domain_size_mean"],
                          yerr=sub["mean_domain_size_std"],
                          marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                          color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                          label=geom, capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=6)
        axes[1].errorbar(sub["Q_mean"], sub["n_domains_mean"],
                          yerr=sub["n_domains_std"],
                          marker=GEOM_MARKERS.get(geom, "o"),
                          color=GEOM_COLORS.get(geom, None),
                          label=geom, capsize=3, lw=1.5, ms=6)

    for ax, ylabel, title in zip(
            axes,
            ["mean domain size (no. of needles)", "number of domains"],
            ["Mean domain size vs. Q", "Number of domains vs. Q"]):
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.set_xlabel(r"$Q = \omega_0 I / b$")
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.axvline(1.0, color="gray", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
        ax.legend(title="Geometry")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(out_path, dpi=150)
    plt.close(fig)


def rebuild_manifest_from_files(sweep_dir):
    """
    Rebuilds the manifest DataFrame from the JSON/CSV files in the sweep directory
    when manifest.csv is missing.
    Compatible with outputs from damping_sweep.py, damping_sweepV02.py, and sweep_damping_hysteresis.py.
    """
    import glob
    json_paths = glob.glob(os.path.join(sweep_dir, "**", "*.json"), recursive=True)
    if not json_paths:
        return None

    rows = []
    for jp in json_paths:
        try:
            with open(jp) as f:
                meta = json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            continue

        geometry = meta.get("geometry", "")
        seed = meta.get("seed", np.nan)
        damping = meta.get("damping", np.nan)
        Q = meta.get("Q", meta.get("Q_target", np.nan))
        stage = meta.get("field_mode", "")

        # Infer stage if not explicit
        if not stage:
            if "relax" in jp or "static" in jp:
                stage = "relax"
            else:
                stage = "hysteresis"
        elif stage == "static_relax":
            stage = "relax"

        # Try to locate the respective CSV file
        base_no_ext = os.path.splitext(jp)[0]
        if base_no_ext.endswith("_hyst"):
            base_no_ext = base_no_ext[:-5]
        elif base_no_ext.endswith("_relax"):
            base_no_ext = base_no_ext[:-6]

        csv_path = base_no_ext + ".csv"
        if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
            filename = os.path.basename(csv_path)
            parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(jp))
            cand_hyst = os.path.join(parent_dir, "hysteresis", filename)
            cand_relax = os.path.join(parent_dir, "relax", filename)
            if os.path.exists(cand_hyst):
                csv_path = cand_hyst
            elif os.path.exists(cand_relax):
                csv_path = cand_relax
            else:
                continue

        tag = os.path.basename(base_no_ext)
        rows.append({
            "tag": tag,
            "stage": stage,
            "geometry": geometry,
            "seed": int(seed) if not np.isnan(seed) else seed,
            "damping": damping,
            "Q": Q,
            "csv_path": csv_path,
            "meta_path": jp,
            "n_steps": meta.get("n_steps", meta.get("n_steps_logged", np.nan)),
            "wall_seconds": meta.get("wall_seconds", meta.get("wall_time_seconds", np.nan))
        })

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if len(df) == 0:
        return None

    # Reconstruct damp_idx by sorting the unique values of Q per geometry and stage
    df["damp_idx"] = 0
    for (geom, stg), grp in df.groupby(["geometry", "stage"]):
        unique_Qs = sorted(grp["Q"].dropna().unique(), reverse=True)
        q_to_idx = {q: idx for idx, q in enumerate(unique_Qs)}
        df.loc[grp.index, "damp_idx"] = grp["Q"].map(q_to_idx).fillna(0).astype(int)

    return df


# main
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                  formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--sweep_dir", type=str, required=True,
                     help="Directory passed as --out_dir to damping_sweep.py")
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--mad_threshold", type=float, default=4.0,
                     help="Threshold (in multiples of MAD) for avalanche detection in dM/dB")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    manifest_path = os.path.join(args.sweep_dir, "manifest.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(manifest_path):
        print(f"Warning: manifest.csv not found in {args.sweep_dir}. Attempting to rebuild from JSON files...")
        manifest = rebuild_manifest_from_files(args.sweep_dir)
        if manifest is None or len(manifest) == 0:
            print(f"ERROR: Could not find or reconstruct manifest from files in {args.sweep_dir}")
            sys.exit(1)
        print(f"Manifest successfully reconstructed from {len(manifest)} JSON/CSV files.")
    else:
        manifest = pd.read_csv(manifest_path)

    hyst_rows = manifest[manifest["stage"] == "hysteresis"]
    relax_rows = manifest[manifest["stage"] == "relax"]

    print(f"Manifest: {len(hyst_rows)} hysteresis runs, "
          f"{len(relax_rows)} relaxation runs.")

    summary_df = pd.DataFrame()
    relax_df = pd.DataFrame()

    # ── Stage 1: process each hysteresis run ──────────────────────
    if len(hyst_rows) > 0:
        print("\nProcessing hysteresis runs (area, Bc, Mr, avalanches, MLE)...")
        hyst_results = []
        for i, (_, row) in enumerate(hyst_rows.iterrows()):
            print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(hyst_rows)}] {row['tag']}", end="\r")
            hyst_results.append(process_hysteresis_run(row, args.mad_threshold))
        print()

        summary_df = pd.DataFrame(hyst_results)
        if "avalanche_sizes" in summary_df.columns:
            summary_csv = summary_df.drop(columns=["avalanche_sizes"])
        else:
            summary_csv = summary_df
        summary_csv_path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, "summary_hysteresis.csv")
        summary_csv.to_csv(summary_csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Saved: {summary_csv_path}")

        # ── power-law fitting: aggregates avalanches across seeds BEFORE
        #    running MLE for each (geometry, damp_idx) point -- see function docstring.
        print("\nFitting power law (avalanches aggregated across seeds)...")
        tau_df = fit_powerlaw_per_geom_damp(summary_df)
        tau_csv_path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, "powerlaw_fits.csv")
        tau_df.to_csv(tau_csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Saved: {tau_csv_path}")
        print(tau_df.to_string(index=False))

        # ── aggregates (mean+std across seeds) of loop metrics ──────────
        print("\nGenerating hysteresis plots...")
        agg_loop = aggregate_by_geom_damp(summary_df, ["area", "Bc", "Mr"])
        agg_loop.to_csv(os.path.join(args.out_dir, "aggregated_loop_metrics.csv"), index=False)

        plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_loop, "area", "hysteresis loop area  [T]",
                          "Loop area vs. quality factor",
                          os.path.join(args.out_dir, "area_vs_Q.png"))
        plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_loop, "Bc", r"coercive field $B_c$  [T]",
                          "Coercive field vs. quality factor",
                          os.path.join(args.out_dir, "Bc_vs_Q.png"))
        plot_metric_vs_Q(agg_loop, "Mr", r"remanence $M_r$",
                          "Remanence vs. quality factor",
                          os.path.join(args.out_dir, "Mr_vs_Q.png"))

        # ── central plot: tau(Q) ─────────────────────────────────────
        plot_tau_vs_Q(tau_df, os.path.join(args.out_dir, "tau_vs_Q.png"))

        # ── avalanche histograms (visual, selected geometries/Q) ─────────
        plot_avalanche_histograms(summary_df, os.path.join(args.out_dir, "avalanche_histograms.png"))
    else:
        print("\nNo hysteresis runs found.")

    # ── Stage 2: process each relaxation run ───────────────────────
    if len(relax_rows) > 0:
        print("\nProcessing relaxation runs (domain statistics)...")
        relax_results = [process_relax_run(row) for _, row in relax_rows.iterrows()]
        relax_df = pd.DataFrame(relax_results)
        relax_csv_path = os.path.join(args.out_dir, "summary_relax.csv")
        relax_df.to_csv(relax_csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"Saved: {relax_csv_path}")

        # ── domains vs Q ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        plot_domain_stats_vs_Q(relax_df, os.path.join(args.out_dir, "domain_size_vs_Q.png"))
    else:
        print("\nNo relaxation runs found.")

    print(f"\nCompleted. Results in: {args.out_dir}")
    print("Generated files:")
    files_to_print = []
    if not summary_df.empty:
        files_to_print += ["summary_hysteresis.csv", "aggregated_loop_metrics.csv", "powerlaw_fits.csv",
                           "area_vs_Q.png", "Bc_vs_Q.png", "Mr_vs_Q.png", "tau_vs_Q.png", "avalanche_histograms.png"]
    if not relax_df.empty:
        files_to_print += ["summary_relax.csv", "domain_size_vs_Q.png"]
    for fname in files_to_print:
        print(f"  - {fname}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
